memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not approach a woman to have sexual relations during the uncleanness of her monthly period. Do not have sexual relations with your neighbour's wife and defile yourself with her.'" - Lev 18:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two commands here, and both concern how we treat another person.

The first assumes the honour of a woman's body and its rhythms — that a husband is not simply to take what he wants when he wants it. Even within marriage, God places limits. That in itself was countercultural in a world where a wife's body was often considered her husband's property.

The second is adultery, and God's reasoning is worth noticing: your neighbour's wife. She is not only a woman; she belongs within another marriage, another home, another set of relationships. Adultery is never a private matter between two consenting people. It reaches into a family.

Both commands share a principle. Other people are not resources for our desire. They have a dignity that limits what we may do, even when we want to, even when we could.

Jesus took this further than any law had. Anyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart (Matt 5:28). He moved the boundary from behaviour to the imagination — not to make us despair, but to show that this has always been a matter of the heart.

Which means the answer is never mere willpower. It is a heart changed by grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat others as people to be honoured, or as objects for your desire?
2. Where do your thoughts need God's attention, not just your actions?
3. What practical step would help you guard your heart this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my heart and my eyes. Teach me to see people as those You have made and honour them, and change me from the inside where willpower cannot reach. Amen.
